newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says firm itself may be involved in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says firm itself may be involved in scandal.

text.p: The president of scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Junichi Ujiie, said on Friday that he would not deny the possibility that the Japanese brokerage itself had been involved in a racketeer payoff scandal if the firm was so accused.

Ujiie was speaking at a news conference after the arrest earlier on Friday of former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki. Prosecutors said they had arrested Sakamaki on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in March 1995.
Ujiie took over as president in early May after Masashi Suzuki, who succeeded Sakamaki on March 14, stepped down.

Ujiie said he would not deny that the company itself was involved in the scandal if the arrest of Sakamaki was regarded as a result of the company's involvement in the scandal. But he said if people said that all Nomura and executives and officials were involved in the scandal, that would not be true.
Ujiie said Nomura had asked Sakamaki to resign as an adviser to the company to take social responsibility for the scandal.

Asked if Nomura would request former chairman Setsuya Tabuchi and former president Yoshihisa Tabuchi (no relation) to resign as advisers, Ujiie said the company was considering doing so but had not yet reached a decision.

Ujiie said Sakamaki had told him four or five days ago that he had not been involved in the payoff scandal. Ujiie said he did not have any evidence to show whether what Sakamaki told him was true or not, even though Sakamaki had been arrested.
Ujiie, who became president on May 1, said his most urgent task was to restore the confidence of investors and shareholders in Nomura.

Asked what impact the scandal and the arrest of Sakamaki would have on Nomura's earnings, he said he could not say what the impact would be because the authhorities had not yet decided penalties against Nomura and partly because administrative penalties by the Finance Ministry had not yet been announced.
